intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon-era palace while dressed in traditional Hanbok attire. Rent a Hanbok from one of the many shops near the palace gates for free entry and stunning photo opportunities within the palace grounds. Arrive early afternoon to make the most of Day 2 after a late Day 1 arrival. Stay in Jongno-gu area hotels to walk to this attraction.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most beloved traditional markets. Sample iconic local dishes including bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). This is a quintessential local food experience beloved by both residents and visitors. Staying in Jongno-gu puts you within easy walking or one-stop subway distance.

experiences.name: HYBE Insight Museum & K-Pop Idol District Walk
experiences.description: Visit the HYBE Insight museum, the official exhibition space of HYBE Entertainment (home of BTS and other top K-pop acts), featuring immersive displays, rare memorabilia, and interactive K-pop experiences. Afterward, explore the surrounding Yongsan area known for its K-pop shops, entertainment agency buildings, and fan culture hotspots. Book tickets in advance online to secure entry.

experiences.name: Insadong Cultural Street & Ssamziegil Courtyard
experiences.description: Stroll through Insadong's charming traditional arts street lined with tea houses, antique shops, Korean craft galleries, and street food stalls. Explore the unique Ssamziegil open-air courtyard mall featuring indie Korean designers and artisan goods. End with a traditional Korean tea ceremony at one of the historic teahouses. This area is walkable from Jongno-gu hotels, making it ideal for a relaxed mid-trip cultural afternoon.

experiences.name: Hongdae K-Culture Night Experience
experiences.description: Spend an evening in Hongdae, Seoul's vibrant youth and K-culture hub. Enjoy live busking performances by aspiring K-pop artists, browse K-pop merchandise stores, visit a norebang (private karaoke room) for a classic Korean night out, and dine at trendy local eateries. The area is lively from early evening and is best experienced after 18:00. Take the subway directly from Jongno-gu in under 30 minutes.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit from Incheon Airport to Jongno-gu via AREX Express Train (approx. 43 min, ~₩9,500). Check in to boutique stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into accommodation, grab a local convenience store snack (GS25 or CU), then take a short walk to explore the immediate Jongno-gu neighborhood. Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace exterior and Gwanghwamun Square (free to walk around) to get your first feel of Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Insadong Alley for your first K-culture immersion — browse traditional craft shops, street art, and lantern-lit alleys. Grab dinner at a nearby pojangmacha (street food tent).

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Convenience store kimbap and ramyeon (~₩3,000–5,000) after check-in
meals.dinner: Insadong street food — tteokbokki, hotteok, and odeng skewers (~₩5,000–8,000)

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a T-money card at the airport or any convenience store (~₩3,000 card + top up ₩20,000) for seamless subway and bus travel throughout the trip. December in Seoul is cold (0–5°C), so layer up with thermal wear.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (₩3,000 admission) when it opens at 9:00. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 and 14:00. Wear or rent a hanbok at the palace entrance for free entry and great photo opportunities (~₩15,000–20,000 rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village (free) — a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Explore the winding alleys and enjoy panoramic views over the city. Continue to Samcheongdong-gil street for window shopping and café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Cheonggyecheon Stream (free) for a peaceful evening walk along the illuminated waterway — especially magical in winter. End the night in nearby Jongno 3-ga with a visit to a local makgeolli bar.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store egg sandwich and canned coffee (~₩3,500)
meals.lunch: Bibimbap at a local Samcheongdong restaurant (~₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Sundubu-jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a Jongno-gu local eatery (~₩7,000–9,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays, so Wednesday is perfect. Hanbok rental shops open around 9:00–10:00. Bukchon is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (Line 2, ~25 min from Jongno). Explore Hongik University Street, the heart of Korean youth culture, indie music, and street art. Browse the vibrant murals and quirky shops in the morning before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Trick Eye Museum area and explore Hongdae's many K-pop merchandise stores and indie boutiques. Head to the nearby Mangwon Market for an authentic local market experience with cheap street food.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Hongdae for the nightlife — catch a free busking performance on the main street (especially lively on weekends). Explore the neon-lit alleys and grab Korean fried chicken and beer (chimaek) at a local pojangmacha.

meals.breakfast: Café toast set in Hongdae (~₩5,000–7,000)
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market street food — bindaetteok (mung bean pancake) and gimbap (~₩5,000–7,000)
meals.dinner: Chimaek (fried chicken + beer) at a Hongdae pojangmacha (~₩12,000–15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is a must for K-culture lovers — check local event boards for indie concerts or pop-up K-pop events. Mangwon Market is a 10-minute walk from Hongdae station.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Changdeokgung Palace and the Secret Garden (Huwon) — book the Secret Garden tour in advance (₩8,000 total). The palace is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Seoul's most beautiful. Tours run at set times; English tour at 11:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ikseon-dong Hanok Village, a trendy neighborhood blending traditional hanok architecture with modern cafés and vintage shops. Perfect for K-culture photography and budget café hopping.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a stunning futuristic landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. The exterior is free to explore and beautifully lit at night. Browse the nearby Dongdaemun Market for budget fashion and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotteok (sweet pancake) from a street stall near the hotel (~₩1,500)
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong café lunch set — Korean fusion rice bowl (~₩9,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun Market food stalls — ddeokbokki, sundae, twigim combo (~₩5,000–7,000)

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours have limited spots — book online at the official palace website. DDP is open late and the surrounding market area is busiest after 22:00 — great for night owls.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park (free entry) — take Bus 704 from Jongno. Hike the Bukhansanseong Fortress Trail (beginner-friendly, ~2–3 hours) for stunning winter views of Seoul surrounded by ancient fortress walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a quieter, more local alternative to Bukchon with independent bookshops, art galleries, and traditional tea houses. Explore at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwangjang Market (Line 1, Jongno 5-ga) — one of Seoul's oldest and most famous traditional markets. This is a foodie paradise with iconic bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and raw beef yukhoe.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store triangle kimbap and banana milk (~₩2,500)
meals.lunch: Packed kimbap from convenience store or trail snacks (~₩3,000)
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market feast — bindaetteok + mayak gimbap + makgeolli (~₩10,000–13,000)

day_by_day.notes: Wear warm, layered hiking clothes for Bukhansan — December temperatures on the mountain can drop to -5°C or below. Gwangjang Market is extremely popular on weekends — arrive by 18:00 to avoid the longest queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (free, walking distance from hotel in Jongno) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated in winter. Attend the morning bell ceremony if available and explore the serene temple grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Tapgol Park and explore the Jongno area's historical sites. Then take the subway to Namdaemun Market (Line 4, Hoehyeon station) — Seoul's largest traditional market for budget shopping: street food, clothing, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Myeongdong (5-min walk from Namdaemun) for a classic Seoul evening. Browse K-beauty shops for budget skincare hauls and enjoy the famous Myeongdong street food alley with skewers, egg bread, and lobster tails.

meals.breakfast: Juk (Korean porridge) at a Jongno local restaurant (~₩7,000–9,000)
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) (~₩7,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food crawl — gyeran-bbang (egg bread), hotteok, skewers (~₩8,000–10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is especially atmospheric in winter with lantern decorations. Myeongdong K-beauty shops often have buy-one-get-one deals — great for budget souvenir shopping. Bring a tote bag.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Itaewon (Line 6) and explore the multicultural neighborhood in the morning when it's quiet. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (₩10,000) for world-class Korean and contemporary art collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) — hike the Namsan trail (free) or take the cable car (₩9,500 round trip). Enjoy panoramic winter views of Seoul from the observation deck (₩16,000). Add a love lock to the famous fence.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Itaewon for dinner and explore the diverse restaurant scene. Walk through the quieter Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood — a local expat and artist community with great budget eateries and bars.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near Itaewon station (~₩6,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Budget Korean set meal near Itaewon (~₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Haebangchon local restaurant — Korean army stew (budae-jjigae) (~₩10,000–12,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Namsan Tower observation deck is best visited around sunset (around 17:00–17:30 in December) for both daylight and night city views. The hiking trail up Namsan takes about 30–40 minutes and is free.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (1 hour by subway/bus from Seoul, ~₩1,500 fare). The UNESCO-listed fortress walls offer a stunning winter walk with mountain and city views. Admission to the fortress is ₩1,000.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's old town around the fortress — visit the Hwaseong Haenggung Palace (₩1,500) and the traditional Paldalmun Market for local Suwon galbi (grilled short ribs), famous throughout Korea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul by 18:00–19:00. Relax in the Jongno area and visit a local jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) for a budget wellness experience — great for tired legs after a day of walking.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast before departure (~₩3,000)
meals.lunch: Suwon galbi (grilled short ribs) at Paldalmun Market — iconic local dish (~₩12,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Simple doenjang-jjigae (soybean paste stew) set at a Jongno local restaurant (~₩7,000–9,000)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is a fantastic half-day trip easily done independently. A jjimjilbang near Jongno costs around ₩10,000–15,000 for entry and includes access to hot baths, sauna rooms, and sleeping areas — a quintessential Korean experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea (free, inside Gyeongbokgung grounds) — an excellent introduction to Korean history, traditions, and daily life across the centuries. Perfect for a cold morning indoors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Anguk neighborhood and visit the Unhyeongung Palace (₩1,000) — a smaller, less-visited royal residence with a peaceful atmosphere. Then walk to the nearby Korean craft shops and art galleries along Insadong.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free K-culture walking tour (check platforms like Airbnb Experiences or local free tour operators) or explore Jongno's pojangmacha street food scene for a festive pre-Christmas evening with locals.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a Jongno local diner — doenjang-jjigae and rice (~₩6,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong traditional tea house lunch — tteok (rice cake) set (~₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Pojangmacha near Jongno 3-ga — soondae (blood sausage), tteokbokki, makgeolli (~₩8,000–10,000)

day_by_day.notes: The National Folk Museum has excellent English signage and is free of charge. Check Airbnb Experiences or Meetup Seoul for free or low-cost K-culture events happening around Christmas week.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (₩27,000) in Jamsil for breathtaking views of Seoul — on a clear winter day you can see for miles. The tower is the 5th tallest in the world. Nearby Lotte World Mall is free to browse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Olympic Park (free) nearby — a large green space with public art installations and the KSPO Dome. Walk along the peaceful winter paths and visit the Seoul Olympic Museum (₩3,000).
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul! Head to Myeongdong or Cheonggyecheon Stream for festive illuminations and Christmas markets. Seoul has a vibrant Christmas atmosphere — enjoy street performances, hot drinks, and festive street food.

meals.breakfast: Café brunch near Jamsil (~₩8,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Olympic Park area convenience store or packed lunch (~₩4,000–5,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Christmas street food + a warm bowl of ramyeon at a local restaurant (~₩10,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is a big celebration in Seoul — the city is beautifully decorated. Book any restaurant dinner in advance if you want a sit-down meal, as popular spots fill up quickly. Cheonggyecheon Stream illuminations are free and stunning.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Gangnam (Line 2) and explore the famous Gangnam district — walk along Garosu-gil (tree-lined avenue) with its boutique shops and cafés. Visit the COEX Starfield Library (free) inside COEX Mall — one of Seoul's most photogenic spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the COEX Aquarium (₩29,000) or browse the massive COEX Mall for free. Walk to nearby Bongeunsa Temple (₩3,000) — a 1,200-year-old Buddhist temple strikingly set among Gangnam's skyscrapers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jongno for a relaxed Christmas dinner at a Korean BBQ restaurant — splurge slightly for the occasion. Samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly) with soju is a beloved Korean Christmas tradition.

meals.breakfast: Garosu-gil brunch café (~₩9,000–11,000)
meals.lunch: COEX food court — Korean set meal (~₩9,000–11,000)
meals.dinner: Korean BBQ (samgyeopsal + soju) near Jongno — slight budget splurge (~₩15,000–20,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea — most attractions remain open. Bongeunsa Temple is especially serene on Christmas Day with fewer tourists. The COEX Starfield Library is free and perfect for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea (free entry) in Yongsan — one of the most impressive and moving museums in Asia. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the extensive indoor and outdoor exhibits covering Korean War history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Yongsan Electronics Market — a massive complex of electronics and tech shops, great for budget gadgets, phone accessories, and K-pop merchandise. Then explore the nearby Haebangchon neighborhood for local café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for a final lively evening — catch street busking performances, browse K-pop merchandise stores, and enjoy the vibrant nightlife. Visit a norebang (karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture experience (~₩10,000–15,000/hour per room).

meals.breakfast: Jongno convenience store or local bakery (~₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Yongsan area Korean restaurant — bibimbap or dosirak (lunch box) set (~₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae local restaurant — japchae and pajeon (scallion pancake) with makgeolli (~₩10,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is free and genuinely world-class — allow at least 2.5 hours. Norebang is a must-do K-culture activity — rooms are rented by the hour and shared with your group, making it very affordable.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite Jongno neighborhood spots for last-minute photos. Pick up souvenirs at Insadong (traditional crafts, hanji paper goods, K-snacks) or Namdaemun Market for budget gifts. Visit Jogyesa Temple one last time for a peaceful send-off.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Incheon Airport via AREX Express Train from Seoul Station (₩9,500, ~43 min). Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before departure for international flights. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Korean snacks and cosmetics.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon Airport. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — haejang-guk (hangover soup) or kongnamul-gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) at a Jongno local restaurant (~₩7,000–9,000)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience store before departure (~₩8,000–10,000)
meals.dinner: Meal on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time at Incheon Airport — it is massive and beautiful (worth arriving early to explore). Pack Korean snacks like honey butter chips, Choco Pie, and Pepero as gifts. Keep ₩10,000–15,000 in T-money for the airport train fare. Total estimated daily budget: ₩40,000–70,000 (approx. $30–55 USD) excluding accommodation.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and take the AREX Express Train (~43 min) to Seoul Station. Check in to your Boutique Stay in Jongno-gu (approx. 15:00–15:30). Freshen up and take a gentle orientation stroll around Insadong alley — browse antique shops, traditional crafts, and street art to get your first feel of Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Cheonggyecheon Stream (청계천) for a relaxing evening stroll along the illuminated waterway. The winter light festival decorations make it especially magical in December. Wind down nearby.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Seoul Station — try a convenience store kimbap set (GS25 or CU) for an authentic fast intro to Korean snacks (~₩3,000–5,000)
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung — warming ginseng chicken soup perfect for a cold December arrival (~₩18,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag is real. Exchange some currency at the airport (KEB Hana Bank counter) or use a Wise/Revolut card. Pick up a T-money card at any convenience store for seamless subway travel.

day_by_day.morning: Start with Gyeongbokgung Palace (경복궁) — arrive early (~09:00) to watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (held at 10:00 and 14:00). Rent a hanbok at a nearby rental shop (₩15,000–20,000/2hrs) for free palace entry and stunning photos against the traditional architecture and snow-dusted rooftops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village (북촌 한옥마을) — wander the narrow lanes lined with traditional Korean houses. Then explore Samcheongdong-gil (삼청동길), a charming street full of independent galleries, cafés, and boutiques. Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea inside the palace grounds (~₩3,000).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square (광화문광장) to see the Yi Sun-sin statue and seasonal winter installations. Explore the nearby underground Gwanghwamun shopping arcade for warmth and local browsing.

meals.breakfast: Café Bora (카페 보라) in Insadong — famous for purple taro soft-serve and traditional tea; grab a light Korean breakfast set (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Gyeongbokgung area pojangmacha (street food stall) — tteokbokki, hotteok, and odeng (fish cake skewers) (~₩5,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Gwanghwamun Gukbap (광화문국밥) — hearty pork rice soup, a Seoul institution; affordable and deeply satisfying in winter (~₩10,000–13,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — Wednesday is perfect. Wear warm layers; December temperatures in Seoul range from -5°C to 5°C. The hanbok experience is highly recommended for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (창덕궁) and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (후원 — Huwon). Book the Secret Garden tour in advance online (~₩8,000). The frozen pond and bare winter trees create an ethereal atmosphere. Nearby Changgyeonggung Palace can be explored as a bonus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ikseon-dong Hanok Village (익선동) — Seoul's trendiest retro neighborhood with hanok buildings converted into indie cafés, vintage clothing stores, and fusion restaurants. Very close to your Jongno-gu hotel. Browse at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Jongmyo Shrine (종묘) — a serene UNESCO World Heritage Site, the royal ancestral shrine of the Joseon Dynasty. Then walk along Jongno (종로) street for evening energy and neon lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery — Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for a Korean-style morning pastry and coffee (~₩6,000–9,000)
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong — try one of the fusion hanok cafés for a bibimbap or Korean brunch set (~₩12,000–16,000)
meals.dinner: Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha alley — outdoor tent restaurants serving grilled meats, soondae (blood sausage), and makgeolli (rice wine). An authentic, lively local experience (~₩15,000–20,000 with drinks)

day_by_day.notes: Ikseon-dong is extremely photogenic and very close to your accommodation — ideal for a relaxed afternoon. Book Changdeokgung Secret Garden online at heritage.go.kr as spots are limited.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Namsangol Hanok Village (남산골 한옥마을) at the base of Namsan Mountain — a free open-air museum of restored traditional homes with winter cultural performances. Then take the Namsan Cable Car (~₩12,000 round trip) up to N Seoul Tower (남산타워).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore N Seoul Tower observation deck (~₩21,000) for panoramic views of the city. Browse the love lock fence and the digital art installations inside. Descend via the scenic walking trail (Namsan둘레길) if weather permits — about 40 minutes downhill through pine forest.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Myeongdong (명동) — Seoul's famous shopping and street food district. Explore the outdoor market stalls selling hotteok, egg bread, lobster skewers, and tornado potatoes. Great for skincare shopping at Innisfree, Etude House, and The Face Shop.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market (광장시장) morning visit — bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and mayak gimbap (addictive mini rolls). A Seoul must-do (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Near Namsan — Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자) for handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) and mandu (dumplings). Always a queue but worth it (~₩11,000–14,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food dinner — budget ₩10,000–15,000 grazing across multiple stalls for a fun, casual, very Korean experience

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong is extremely popular with tourists but the street food and skincare shopping are genuinely excellent. Go on a Friday evening for peak atmosphere. N Seoul Tower is beautiful at night.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP — 동대문디자인플라자) — Zaha Hadid's futuristic landmark. Check the current exhibitions (usually ₩5,000–10,000). The surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park has remnants of the old Seoul city wall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Naksan Park (낙산공원) trail — a hillside park following the ancient Seoul fortress wall with great city views and street murals. Descend into Ihwa-dong Mural Village (이화동 벽화마을) for colorful public art and indie cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Dongdaemun Fashion Town — the massive 24-hour wholesale and retail fashion market complex (Doota, Migliore, Hello apM). Saturdays are especially lively. Great for affordable Korean fashion finds.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café in Jongno-gu — try a traditional Korean breakfast of doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean soup) and rice at a local bunsik restaurant (~₩7,000–9,000)
meals.lunch: Ihwa-dong area café lunch — a warm bowl of doenjang jjigae or ramyeon at a cozy hillside café (~₩10,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — Pyounghwa Market basement food court for authentic Korean comfort food: galbi tang (short rib soup), japchae, and banchan spread (~₩12,000–16,000)

day_by_day.notes: DDP is open late and the exterior is stunning when lit up at night. Saturday evening at Dongdaemun is extremely energetic. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Naksan trail involves steps and hills.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located right in Jongno-gu. In December it's decorated with thousands of lanterns for winter festivals. Attend a morning bell ceremony if available. Then visit the nearby Buddhist cultural center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts (세종문화회관) area and check for any Sunday afternoon cultural performances or exhibitions. Walk along the Cheonggyecheon Stream again in daylight for a different perspective, heading east toward the more local sections.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Insadong (인사동) for a Sunday evening market — local artisans, traditional crafts, and street performers. Browse Ssamziegil (쌈지길), an indie courtyard mall with unique Korean designer goods.

meals.breakfast: Insadong tea house breakfast — Dawon (다원) traditional tea house offers Korean rice porridge (juk) and herbal teas in a beautiful hanok setting (~₩10,000–15,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong Ssamziegil food court — try pajeon (green onion pancake) and makgeolli pairing (~₩12,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Sunday is perfect for samgyeopsal — visit Mapo Sutbul Galbi near the Jongno area for premium grilled pork belly with banchan, lettuce wraps, and doenjang jjigae (~₩18,000–25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is free to enter and deeply peaceful — a wonderful contrast to the busy shopping areas. Insadong Sunday market is one of the best in Seoul for authentic crafts and K-culture souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park (북한산국립공원) — take the subway to Gupabal or Dobongsan station. Choose a beginner-friendly trail like the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail (~2–3 hours) for stunning winter mountain views and ancient fortress walls dusted with snow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city by early afternoon. Visit Seodaemun Prison History Hall (서대문형무소역사관) — a sobering and important museum documenting Korea's independence movement and Japanese colonial period (~₩3,000). Essential for understanding Korean history and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hongdae (홍대) neighborhood — Seoul's university arts district, famous for street performances, indie music venues, and youthful energy. Walk the main street and duck into vintage shops and K-indie music bars.

meals.breakfast: Pack convenience store onigiri and hot canned coffee for the mountain trip — very Korean and practical (~₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Post-hike at a Gupabal village restaurant — doenjang jjigae set with rice and banchan, popular with hikers (~₩10,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Hongdae — Yoogane Dak Galbi (유가네 닭갈비) for stir-fried spicy chicken with rice cakes and vegetables cooked at your table (~₩13,000–16,000)

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan in winter requires good footwear — trail crampons (아이젠, ice grippers) can be rented at the trailhead for ~₩3,000. Check trail conditions in advance. Seodaemun closes on Mondays — swap with Tuesday if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums, with an extraordinary collection of Korean artifacts from prehistoric times through the Joseon Dynasty. Free general admission. Allow 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the subway to Itaewon (이태원) — Seoul's most international neighborhood. Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art (리움미술관) for world-class Korean and contemporary art (~₩20,000). Browse Antique Furniture Street and the Haebangchon (HBC) hillside neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Itaewon for the evening — explore the main strip and side streets. Visit a rooftop bar for December skyline views with a warm drink.

meals.breakfast: Jongno-gu local bunsik (분식) restaurant — kimchi jjigae set with rice, a classic Korean morning meal (~₩8,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria — affordable Korean set meals with a view of the beautiful museum garden (~₩10,000–14,000)
meals.dinner: Itaewon — Vatos Urban Tacos for Korean-Mexican fusion (a Seoul cult classic) or a traditional Korean BBQ spot on the main street (~₩18,000–25,000)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is genuinely world-class and completely free for the permanent collection — do not skip it. Leeum Museum has exceptional Korean celadon and contemporary Korean art.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace (경희궁) — a lesser-visited palace near Gwanghwamun, peaceful and crowd-free. Then walk to the Seoul Museum of History (서울역사박물관) next door — free admission, excellent exhibits on Seoul's transformation from Joseon capital to modern megacity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seochon Village (서촌마을) — a charming neighborhood west of Gyeongbokgung, home to artists, writers, and indie cafés in traditional alleyways. Visit Yun Dong-ju Literature House (윤동주문학관) — a beautifully converted water tank honoring Korea's beloved resistance poet.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-Christmas Eve atmosphere in Gwanghwamun and Jongno — Seoul decorates extensively for Christmas. Enjoy the festive lights, street performances, and seasonal markets around City Hall Plaza (서울광장) where an outdoor ice rink is typically set up.

meals.breakfast: Seochon area café — Hyoja-dong traditional café for nurungji (scorched rice tea) and tteok (rice cake) snacks (~₩8,000–11,000)
meals.lunch: Seochon — Tongin Market (통인시장) dosirak café: buy old Korean coins and exchange for tteokbokki, jeon, and various banchan dishes from different stalls. Unique and fun (~₩5,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Gwanghwamun area — Cheongwadae Sarangchae nearby for traditional Korean royal court cuisine-inspired dishes, or a cozy galbi restaurant for pre-Christmas dinner (~₩20,000–28,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tongin Market dosirak experience is one of Seoul's most unique food experiences — highly recommended. Seoul City Hall ice rink is open in December and skate rentals are available (~₩1,000 entry + ₩2,000 rental).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Korean Folk Village (한국민속촌) in Yongin — about 1 hour from Seoul by subway + shuttle. This living open-air museum recreates traditional Korean village life with performances, craftspeople, and seasonal winter activities. Special Christmas-themed Korean cultural events often held.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul by early afternoon. Explore Lotte World (롯데월드) in Jamsil — Asia's largest indoor theme park with an outdoor section. On Christmas Eve it's beautifully decorated. Alternatively, visit the adjacent Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory (롯데월드타워 서울스카이, ~₩29,000) for the highest views in Korea.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major event — Koreans celebrate it as a romantic holiday. Join the festivities in Myeongdong or Gangnam. Attend a candlelight service at Myeongdong Cathedral (명동성당) — Seoul's most iconic Catholic church, stunning in December.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a warm bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) at a Jongno local restaurant — perfect winter morning fuel (~₩12,000–15,000)
meals.lunch: Korean Folk Village food stalls — traditional foods like hoddeok, sikhye (sweet rice drink), and grilled meats in a historical setting (~₩8,000–12,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — book ahead at a mid-range restaurant. Try Gaon (가온) for modern Korean cuisine, or opt for a festive set menu at a Myeongdong restaurant (~₩35,000–50,000 for a special occasion dinner)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of Seoul's busiest nights — book dinner in advance. Myeongdong Cathedral's midnight mass is beautiful but very crowded. Lotte World Tower Sky Observatory offers extraordinary nighttime city views.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning — visit Deoksugung Palace (덕수궁) in the heart of the city. The stone wall road (돌담길) around the palace is one of Seoul's most romantic walks. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony in traditional winter dress. The adjacent Seoul Museum of Art (서울시립미술관) has free exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Gangnam (강남) district — visit COEX Mall (코엑스몰), one of Asia's largest underground malls, including the spectacular Starfield Library (별마당 도서관). Browse the Bongeunsa Temple (봉은사) adjacent to COEX — a 1,200-year-old temple dramatically contrasted against Gangnam skyscrapers.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Gangnam's upscale side — stroll Garosu-gil (가로수길), a tree-lined boulevard of boutique fashion stores, galleries, and restaurants. Christmas evening atmosphere with lights and decorations.

meals.breakfast: Christmas treat — Café Bora or a high-quality hotel brunch near your accommodation (~₩15,000–20,000)
meals.lunch: COEX food hall — wide variety of Korean and international options; try a Korean BBQ set or bibimbap in a sit-down restaurant (~₩14,000–18,000)
meals.dinner: Garosu-gil Christmas dinner — Riviera Maison or a Korean-French fusion restaurant for a special evening meal (~₩30,000–45,000)

day_by_day.notes: Many smaller shops may be closed on Christmas Day but major attractions, malls, and restaurants are open. Bongeunsa Temple on Christmas Day offers a beautiful spiritual contrast. Gangnam subway station is a major hub — very accessible from Jongno-gu.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) in Yongsan — a comprehensive and moving museum covering Korean military history, with particular focus on the Korean War. Free admission. The outdoor sculpture garden features tanks, planes, and monuments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Noryangjin Fish Market (노량진수산시장) — Seoul's famous wholesale fish market. Buy fresh seafood from the market stalls and take it upstairs to a restaurant that will prepare it for you (hoe — Korean-style raw fish). An authentic and memorable experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening exploration of Jongno-gu — your home neighborhood. Walk Pimatgol Alley (피맛골), a historic back alley with old-school Korean restaurants. Visit a norebang (노래방 — private karaoke room) for a quintessential K-culture experience (~₩15,000–20,000/hour for a room).

meals.breakfast: Noryangjin area early morning — authentic haejang-guk (해장국, hangover soup/hearty morning soup) at a local 24-hour restaurant near the fish market (~₩10,000–13,000)
meals.lunch: Noryangjin Fish Market — buy fresh raw fish (hoe) and have it prepared upstairs. Budget ₩30,000–50,000 for a generous seafood feast for two
meals.dinner: Pimatgol Alley, Jongno — traditional Korean pojangmacha experience with grilled skewers, jeon (pancakes), and makgeolli rice wine (~₩15,000–20,000)

day_by_day.notes: Noryangjin Fish Market is best visited for lunch — the freshest catch is available in the morning. Norebang is a must-do K-culture experience — groups of any size can book a private room. Great for a final Saturday night in Seoul.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — revisit your favorite neighborhood, Jongno-gu/Insadong, for last-minute souvenir shopping. Best souvenirs: Korean tea sets, hanji (traditional paper) crafts, gochujang paste sets, Korean beauty products, and traditional ceramics. Visit Namdaemun Market (남대문시장) nearby for wholesale prices on Korean goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — if afternoon/evening departure: take the AREX Express from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport. Allow 3 hours before departure for check-in and security. If late departure: visit Cheonggyecheon Stream one final time for a reflective farewell walk along the waterway that welcomed you on Day 1.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Incheon International Airport. Final Korean meal at the airport — Bibigo restaurant in the departure terminal for a proper bibimbap or bulgogi set as a last taste of Seoul (~₩15,000–20,000).

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — go all-out with a traditional Korean table (한식상) at a Jongno restaurant: rice, soup, grilled fish, kimchi, and 8+ banchan side dishes (~₩12,000–16,000)
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market — galchi jorim (braised hairtail fish) or a classic Korean set meal at the market restaurants (~₩10,000–14,000)
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport Bibigo or Korean Air Lounge — a fitting final Korean meal before departure (~₩15,000–20,000)

day_by_day.notes: AREX Express to Incheon takes 43 minutes from Seoul Station. Return your T-money card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus ₩500 handling fee). Most major Korean airlines and shops at Incheon accept credit cards. Pack Korean snacks (choco pie, honey butter chips, dried seaweed) for the flight home!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — No morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury chauffeur service to Boutique Stay in Jongno-gu (approx. 60–70 min). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around Jongno-gu neighborhood. Stroll through Insadong alley — Seoul's iconic cultural street lined with traditional tea houses, antique galleries, and artisan craft shops. Visit Ssamziegil, a charming open-air cultural complex with indie boutiques and Korean art installations.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mingles (Michelin 2-star) or Jungsik Seoul — experience the pinnacle of modern Korean fine dining with a multi-course tasting menu pairing traditional Korean flavors with contemporary techniques. After dinner, a peaceful night walk along Cheonggyecheon Stream, beautifully illuminated in winter.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack at airport lounge or upon arrival at hotel — hotel welcome refreshment platter
meals.dinner: Mingles or Jungsik Seoul — modern Korean haute cuisine, tasting menu with wine pairing (₩200,000–₩300,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pack light layers — December in Seoul is cold (0°C to 7°C). Request the hotel for a heated room pre-setup and welcome amenities. Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace — the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces. Witness the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (10:00 & 14:00). Explore the palace grounds in traditional Hanbok attire, rented from a premium Hanbok rental boutique nearby (Hanboknam or Gyeongbokgung Hanbok).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds, then walk to Bukchon Hanok Village — a beautifully preserved hilltop neighborhood of traditional Korean Hanok houses. Enjoy a private cultural guide explaining Joseon-era architecture and lifestyle.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Gaon (Michelin 3-star) — Seoul's most prestigious Korean fine dining experience, offering a meticulously curated traditional Korean royal court cuisine tasting menu. Post-dinner, enjoy a private tea ceremony experience at a traditional tea house in Insadong.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — Korean traditional morning set or Western buffet at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tosokchon Samgyetang — legendary ginseng chicken soup restaurant near Gyeongbokgung, favored by locals and royalty alike
meals.dinner: Gaon Restaurant (Michelin 3-star) — royal Korean cuisine tasting menu (₩300,000–₩400,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Gaon well in advance — reservations are extremely limited. Hanbok rental is recommended for 2–3 hours in the morning for the best palace photo experience. Bring hand warmers for outdoor exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day tour of Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) — a stunning 78-acre royal garden with ancient trees, lotus ponds, and pavilions dusted in winter frost. Tours are guided and limited in size, offering an exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Changgyeonggung Palace and head to the nearby Naksan Park for panoramic views of Seoul's old city walls and skyline. Walk a section of the Seoul City Wall (Hanyangdoseong) — a 600-year-old fortress wall winding through the hills of Jongno-gu.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Kwon Sooksoo — an intimate, reservation-only Korean fine dining experience helmed by one of Korea's most celebrated chefs, focusing on seasonal and regional Korean ingredients. Evening visit to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) for its striking Zaha Hadid architecture lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — traditional Korean juk (porridge) set with banchan side dishes
meals.lunch: Lunch at Biwon — elegant Korean cuisine restaurant near Changdeokgung, known for refined traditional dishes in a Hanok setting
meals.dinner: Kwon Sooksoo — private seasonal Korean tasting menu (₩250,000–₩350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours must be booked in advance through the Cultural Heritage Administration of Korea. Wear very warm footwear — the garden paths can be icy in December. DDP often hosts special winter light festivals in December — check the schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Private K-culture immersion experience: Visit the SMTOWN COEX Artium (SM Entertainment's flagship cultural space) or HYBE Insight Museum — an interactive museum dedicated to the global K-pop phenomenon with exclusive behind-the-scenes content, holograms, and curated exhibits on BTS and other artists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Gangnam district — visit Cheongdam-dong, Seoul's ultra-luxury fashion district (Korea's equivalent of Rue Saint-Honoré). Browse flagship stores of Korean luxury brands like Gentle Monster, Tamburins, and Ader Error, alongside international maisons. Visit the Dior or Chanel flagship concept stores unique to Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mosu Seoul (Michelin 2-star) — an innovative, ingredient-driven tasting menu by Chef Ahn Sung-jae blending Korean sensibility with global technique. After dinner, experience Gangnam's vibrant nightlife with a visit to a premium rooftop bar such as Alice Cheongdam or Octagon's VIP lounge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Western-style eggs and pastries with Korean sides
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hanilkwan — a legendary Korean restaurant in Gangnam serving traditional Korean cuisine since 1939, famous for Galbi (short rib) and Bibimbap
meals.dinner: Mosu Seoul (Michelin 2-star) — contemporary tasting menu (₩250,000–₩380,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight Museum requires advance ticket booking online. Cheongdam-dong boutiques are best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Arrange private chauffeur for Gangnam day to avoid taxi hassle.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private cultural excursion to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (45 min from Seoul by private car). Walk the 5.7km fortress wall with a private historian guide, exploring the four main gates, watchtowers, and command posts. Stunning winter landscape views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Suwon Hwaseong Museum for deep historical context, then explore the traditional Korean Folk Village nearby — a living open-air museum with traditional performances, craftsmen at work, and authentic Joseon-era architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Dinner at Jungsik Seoul (Michelin 2-star) — if not visited on Day 1, this is an ideal opportunity. Alternatively, enjoy a premium Korean BBQ experience at Maple Tree House in Itaewon — a refined, upscale Korean BBQ restaurant with premium Hanwoo beef.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Korean traditional set with rice, soup, and banchan
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional restaurant in Suwon — Yeonpo Galbi, famous for its charcoal-grilled short ribs near the fortress
meals.dinner: Maple Tree House (Itaewon) — premium Hanwoo beef Korean BBQ (₩150,000–₩250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Suwon Hwaseong is best explored with a private guide — arrange through your hotel concierge. The fortress walk takes approximately 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Dress in thermal layers — the fortress walls are fully exposed to winter wind.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located in the heart of Jongno-gu. Participate in a private temple morning ritual and meditation session arranged through a cultural concierge. The temple is beautifully decorated with lanterns in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Bukchon Hanok Village area more deeply with a private Hanok architecture tour, then visit the Arario Museum in Space — housed in a 1970s building, one of Seoul's most compelling contemporary art museums. Afterward, walk through Gyeonghuigung Palace, the quietest and most serene of Seoul's palaces.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at La Yeon (Lotte Hotel Seoul, Michelin 3-star) — perched on the 38th floor with sweeping Seoul skyline views, La Yeon serves exquisite Korean royal court cuisine in an elegant setting. One of the most celebrated dining experiences in all of Asia.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — light Korean porridge and seasonal side dishes
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tongin Market — a historic traditional market in Jongno-gu where you can use old copper coins to select traditional Korean street foods from various stalls (a uniquely local experience even for luxury travelers)
meals.dinner: La Yeon, Lotte Hotel Seoul (Michelin 3-star) — Korean royal court cuisine tasting menu with city views (₩300,000–₩450,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Temple meditation sessions at Jogyesa should be booked through the temple's cultural program office or hotel concierge. La Yeon is one of the hardest reservations in Seoul — book 4–6 weeks in advance. Tongin Market is a beloved local gem worth experiencing despite its casual nature.

day_by_day.morning: Private K-beauty and wellness morning: Visit Sulwhasoo Flagship Store in Insadong or Amore Pacific Headquarters for an exclusive luxury Korean skincare consultation and personalized product experience. Follow with a premium Korean jjimjilbang (bathhouse) experience at Siloam Sauna or Dragon Hill Spa — a deeply cultural Korean wellness ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming, lesser-known neighborhood of Hanok homes, independent cafés, and artist studios. Visit the Yoon Dong-ju Literary Museum and browse curated local galleries. Stop at a traditional Korean teahouse for premium Korean teas and rice cakes.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Dooreyoo — a celebrated Michelin-starred restaurant focusing on fermented and seasonal Korean ingredients, offering one of the most intellectually engaging Korean dining experiences in the city. Post-dinner, evening stroll through Gwanghwamun Square, beautifully lit in winter.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Western eggs benedict or Korean set
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cafe Onion Anguk or Bukchon Sonmandoo — artisan dumplings handmade by a grandmother in a tiny Hanok house, a legendary local institution
meals.dinner: Dooreyoo (Michelin-starred) — fermentation-focused Korean tasting menu (₩200,000–₩300,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sulwhasoo Flagship offers complimentary facial treatments with purchase — request an appointment in advance. Siloam Sauna is open 24 hours and is a genuine local cultural experience. Seochon is best explored on foot — wear comfortable but warm shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nami Island and Petite France (2 hours from Seoul by private car) — Nami Island is a picturesque river island famous for its tree-lined paths and serene winter scenery. In December, the island is dusted with frost and decorated for the season, making it exceptionally beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Petite France — a whimsical French-themed cultural village in the mountains near Nami Island. Explore the exhibits on Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's 'The Little Prince' and enjoy the contrast of European aesthetics against Korean mountain scenery. Return toward Seoul via the Garden of Morning Calm (Achim-go-yo Jeongwon) — a stunning botanical garden with its famous winter illumination festival (December).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul. Dinner at Onjium — a prestigious, reservation-only restaurant specializing in the revival of ancient Korean royal and aristocratic recipes, using ingredients and techniques from Joseon-era court cookbooks. A truly rare and historically significant dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant on Nami Island — traditional Korean fare with scenic views
meals.dinner: Onjium — ancient Korean royal cuisine revival tasting menu (₩250,000–₩350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private car and driver for this full-day excursion — public transport is possible but time-consuming. The Garden of Morning Calm Illumination Festival runs November–January and is not to be missed. Book Onjium at least 3–4 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class experience: Join a premium Korean cooking class (arranged through O'ngo Food Communications or a private chef) in a traditional Hanok kitchen. Learn to prepare Kimchi, Bibimbap, Japchae, and traditional Korean soups using seasonal winter ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gyeonggi Museum of Modern Art or the Seoul Museum of History in Jongno-gu for a deep cultural dive into Korean history and contemporary art. Afterward, explore Insa-dong's premium antique and art galleries — an ideal opportunity to acquire authentic Korean celadon pottery, calligraphy scrolls, or traditional paintings as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Eve dinner at Palais de Gaumont or a premium hotel restaurant. Alternatively, a special omakase Korean-Japanese fusion experience at Sushi Saito Seoul or Ryunique — celebrating the festive season with a curated chef's table experience. Evening visit to Namsan Seoul Tower for panoramic night views of the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy a leisurely morning before the cooking class
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared in your cooking class as lunch
meals.dinner: Ryunique or Sushi Saito Seoul — contemporary fusion or Japanese-Korean omakase (₩200,000–₩400,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Premium cooking classes should be booked in advance through the hotel concierge. Namsan Tower is best visited after 18:00 for night views — take the cable car up. Antique shopping in Insadong: budget ₩100,000–₩500,000+ for quality pieces.

day_by_day.morning: Special Christmas Eve morning: Visit Myeongdong Cathedral — Seoul's most iconic Catholic cathedral, beautifully decorated for Christmas. Attend a morning mass or simply admire the architecture and festive atmosphere. Explore Myeongdong neighborhood's luxury shopping streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium shopping afternoon at Lotte Department Store Main Branch (Myeongdong) or Shinsegae Department Store — Korea's oldest and most prestigious department stores. Explore curated Korean luxury goods, designer collaborations, and premium Korean beauty brands. Visit the gourmet food halls for premium Korean snacks and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve dinner at a premium hotel restaurant — consider Aria at the Grand Hyatt Seoul with panoramic city views, or a private chef's table experience at your boutique hotel. After dinner, join the festive Christmas Eve atmosphere in Myeongdong or Cheonggyecheon Stream, beautifully lit with seasonal illuminations.

meals.breakfast: Special hotel Christmas breakfast — festive spread with Korean and Western options
meals.lunch: Lunch at Myeongdong Kyoja — a legendary noodle and dumpling restaurant, one of Seoul's most beloved institutions since 1969
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special dinner at Aria, Grand Hyatt Seoul — panoramic Seoul views with festive tasting menu (₩300,000–₩500,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Seoul is a major celebration — the city is beautifully decorated and lively. Book Christmas Eve dinner well in advance as all premium restaurants fill up months ahead. Myeongdong is extremely crowded on Christmas Eve — enjoy the festive energy but keep valuables secure.

day_by_day.morning: Peaceful Christmas morning: Private sunrise visit to Naksan Park or Bugaksan Mountain trail for a serene winter morning walk above the city. Enjoy the quiet beauty of Seoul's traditional neighborhoods blanketed in winter stillness.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea (Yongsan) — one of Asia's largest and most impressive museums, housing over 220,000 artifacts spanning Korean history from prehistoric times to the Joseon dynasty. Enjoy a private guided tour of the highlights. Afterward, explore the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — a world-class private art museum with exceptional Korean traditional and contemporary collections.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Day dinner at Jungsik Seoul or a premium hotel restaurant. Alternatively, experience a traditional Korean royal banquet recreation dinner arranged through a cultural dining experience company. End the evening with a private rooftop champagne toast overlooking Seoul's glittering skyline.

meals.breakfast: Festive in-hotel Christmas breakfast — special holiday menu with champagne
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sigol Bapsang — a cozy, authentic Korean home-style restaurant serving traditional countryside Korean food, a comforting contrast to fine dining
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul or a private chef's table Christmas dinner — festive tasting menu (₩300,000–₩500,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Many attractions have reduced hours on Christmas Day — confirm opening times in advance. The National Museum of Korea is free to enter (permanent collection). Leeum Museum requires advance ticket booking. Arrange champagne and a rooftop setup through your hotel concierge for a memorable Christmas night.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) — one of the most historically significant and surreal experiences available to visitors in Korea. A private luxury DMZ tour includes visits to the Third Infiltration Tunnel, Dora Observatory (overlooking North Korea), and Dorasan Station — the last train station before the border.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul. Visit Hongdae neighborhood — Seoul's vibrant arts university district, known for its indie music scene, street art, creative boutiques, and youthful energy. Explore the Hongdae Free Market (weekends) and visit a premium vinyl record shop or local art gallery.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner drinks at a rooftop bar — try Charles H. at the Four Seasons Seoul or Sky Bar at Signiel Seoul (floors 76–81 of Lotte World Tower) for extraordinary panoramic views. Dinner at Mingles (Michelin 2-star) — if not visited on Day 1, a must-experience for the final nights in Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before DMZ departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Imjingak Pyeonghwa-Nuri Park near the DMZ — traditional Korean lunch set in a historically poignant setting
meals.dinner: Mingles (Michelin 2-star) — modern Korean tasting menu with wine pairing (₩200,000–₩350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: DMZ tours require advance booking through a licensed tour operator — passport is mandatory. Tours depart early (07:30–08:00) from central Seoul. Photography restrictions apply at certain DMZ sites. Hongdae is most vibrant in the afternoon and evening on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Seoul. Enjoy a slow, indulgent hotel breakfast. Last-minute shopping at Insadong or Gwangjang Market — visit Gwangjang Market for a final immersion into Seoul's most authentic traditional food market: bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, and raw beef yukhoe are iconic must-tries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the boutique stay. Private luxury chauffeur transfer to Incheon International Airport (allow 90 minutes for transfer + check-in). Enjoy the world-class Incheon Airport facilities — visit the transit cultural zone with traditional Korean art performances, or relax in a premium airport lounge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Carry fond memories of Seoul's extraordinary blend of ancient tradition and modern dynamism.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final hotel breakfast — order everything you loved during the stay
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market street food feast — bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, japchae (₩20,000–₩50,000 total)
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure at Incheon. The airport's transit cultural zone offers free traditional Korean performances and craft demonstrations. Duty-free shopping at Incheon is exceptional — Korean cosmetics, ginseng products, and Korean spirits (soju, makgeolli) make excellent last-minute gifts. Confirm private transfer the night before.
